2025 Excellence in Municipal Information Systems Association Award (ITS award)
notes: Council congratulated staff on being awarded the 2025 Excellence in Municipal Systems Award for the Region of Waterloo's technology solution known as Designing and Delivering a Digital Solution to Enhance Road Safety. The award-winning solution was selected by a panel of representatives from Ontario municipalities. The solution offers a user-friendly, streamlined, end-to-end service for teams working in camera-based enforcement. It also provides expanded service options for residents, including 24/7 digital self-service and secure payment options. The project is an innovative example of the Region delivering on two key priority areas of our Growing with Care strategic plan – providing equitable services and opportunities and building a resilient and future-ready organization. The project’s success was accomplished through extensive collaboration across multiple departments and the award was accepted on behalf of all staff by Helen Hiebert, Business Relationship Manager, Information Technology Services and Theresa Mendler, Manager, Automated Enforcements Programs.

items.title: Waterloo Regional Police Services - Mid-Year Presentation to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo Council
notes:
Mark Crowell, Waterloo Regional Police Chief, provided a presentation on mid-year police service activities. A copy of the presentation is attached to the agenda. He highlighted various ongoing efforts and accomplishments captured in the 2024 annual report including the total calls, types of calls, and types of crimes committed. He further highlighted the police services 2025 priorities which include Stratified Policing and Crime Suppression, Advancing the WR Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, Building Towards Sustainable Staffing, and Innovation and Modernization.

In response to Council, M. Crowell explained that the Community Safety and Well-Being plan's vision is to develop as many response models as possible within our community that do not involve police, but rather rely on mental health and community professionals to address mental health and addition needs when applicable. He further explained that the demand for mental health and addiction responses have not lessened, however, the ability for these response systems to be deployed through the crisis call diversion program has had diminished capacity in the past year due to lack of resources and funding.

M. Crowell confirmed that drug-related monies recovered at a crime scene can be reallocated to community organizations with support programs. He emphasized that continued collaboration with other emergency services is essential, and he noted that that 911 calls for service with the Region are split with 73% are police calls for services, 17% are for paramedic services, and 10% are for fire services.

Responding to Council, M. Crowell clarified that the Stratified Policing Model approach is evidence-based that is focused on enhancing crime analysis and the sharing of information throughout the organization to address high crime areas and needs. The collection of evidence is community based through data from service calls as well as a race and identity-based data collection strategy. He further clarified that the call diversion program was paused on April 1, 2025, due to a lack of funding and the WRPS continue to advocate with the province and are looking to strengthen other diversion pathways with community partners. 

In response to Council, M. Crowell explained that the public safety communication centre will manage all the emergency service calls, contain the emergency response site, real time operation centre, and he expressed support that the modernization provided by the centre will remove inefficiencies and encourage sharing resources. He reiterated the importance of emergency preparedness to ensure that the Region is able to respond effectively when a disaster occurs. He confirmed that police service staff are continually reviewing budgets for savings opportunities. 

M. Crowell explained that there are dedicated resources for specific areas that are meant to address repetitive crime patterns with the objective to decrease overall crime. These specific areas, where WRPS has dedicated resources, include community engagement and youth, street crime, and a team known as the 'Dart Unit'. He noted that these are funded through existing budget.

Responding to Council, M. Crowell acknowledged the justice system is overloaded and that the WRPS is dedicated in establishing diversionary pathways when applicable in the given the situation. He confirmed that electronic key notes are being piloted which will allow for electronic and mobile note taking and that local court rooms continue to permit hybrid testimony depending on the case being considered. He further confirmed that the WRPS will retain the discretion to manage a situation through a lens of compassion and only engage, when necessary, especially when involving individuals experiencing homelessness or mental health distress. He also noted that Intimate partner violence continues to be a concern.

M. Crowell explained that WRPS has been working with retail partners to look at deterrent approaches to avoid the crime from being committed by using modern methods such as a time-delay safe, however, there is caution when considering artificial intelligence options (AI). He explained that AI modernization has privacy implications and the WRPS continues to ensure that all applicable legislation is adhered to. He also explained transparency and open data continues to be a priority and must be maintained when modernizing and establishing efficiencies.

C. James requested that the WRPS be aware of the biases that AI technology can have.

items.title: Stephanie Florence, Waterloo
notes:
Stephanie Florence, Waterloo, expressed concern with the proposed approach for the Arts Fund specifically, that artists have not been included in the discussion on how the Arts Fund should be managed. They stated that the arts have been underfund in Ontario and that artists and local businesses are leaving the Region of Waterloo as there is a lack of resources and funding. 

In response to Council, S. Florence reiterated that they would be supportive of an Arts Council that is led by local artists.

items.title: Eric Almberg, Waterloo
notes:
Eric Almberg, Waterloo, provided a delegation on report PDL-CUL-25-019, Arts Funding In-House Allocation 2025. He highlighted that local artists are significant for vibrant communities. He expressed support for a local artist lead Arts Fund Council. 

Responding to questions, E. Almberg suggested that Region should establish an Arts Council based on community feedback and experiences. 

In response to Council, Rod Regier, Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services, agreed that extensive consultation with the community will be conducted in order to develop and establish the Arts Council.

items.title: Andrew Jacob Rinehart, Waterloo
notes:
Andrew Jacob Rinehart, Waterloo, delegated on the proposed Arts Funding recommendation in report PDL-CUL-25-019, Arts Funding In-House Allocation 2025. They expressed concern that during the KPMG audit that no artists were consulted to provide their feedback. They also provided a proposed amendment to the recommended motion:

"That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve a process to expedite establishing an arts council over the next 18 months, governed and maintained by the artistic community in the region of waterloo that would be responsible for administering the fund permanently, in response to the KPMG arts fund review results, as outlined in report PDL-CUL-25-019 dated June 25 2025, and delegation from artists living and/or working within the waterloo region on June 25, 2025.

The region will commit to providing administrative funding, in addition to funding allocated for arts funding." 

In response to Council, A. Rinehart confirmed that there needs to be an interim solution for artists to receiving funding while an Arts Council is established.

items.title: Remy Renz, Kitchener
notes: Remy Renz, Kitchener, delegated on the proposed Arts Funding recommendation in report PDL-CUL-25-019, Arts Funding In-House Allocation 2025. They requested that Council approve the proposed amendment to the recommended motion as presented by the previous delegation A. Rinehart. They expressed concern with the management of the Region of Waterloo Arts Fund and its lack of transparency with community artists.

items.title: Other Matters Under Committee Of The Whole
PDL-CUL-25-019, Arts Funding In-House Allocation 2025
notes:
Rod Regier, Commissioner Planning, Development & Legislative Services, provided a brief overview of the report PDL-CUL-25-019, Arts Funding In-House Allocation 2025. He noted that report addresses the Council request to identify in-house alternatives. He highlighted that Staff investigated internal opportunities to manage the arts fund and determined that the current resources available would require staff to defer existing projects or add temporary staff complement to help with the administration of the funding. He explained that the cost of administering the funding would be approximately $35,000 for either an external contractor or internal allocation of resources. 

Julian Kingston, Director of Cultural Services, explained that the community foundation that administered the funding in 2024 is unable to continue in that capacity so Staff having been working with several interested external organizations, however, the selection of the external organization would need to go through the confidential government procurement process.

Council suggested that the terms of reference include explicit direction on the composition of the proposed Arts Council and that staff investigate working with area municipal partners to administer the funding by using already established arts funding panels at area municipalities.

In response to Council, R. Regier confirmed that during area municipal consultation no area municipality indicated interest in establishing a partnership. J. Kingston further explained that staff are working on enhanced communication to all area municipalities to ensure that artists from all geographical areas are aware of the opportunity to apply for funding. 

Council acknowledged importance of a simplistic approach to administrating grants for arts funding led by local artists experts and that the distribution of funding to artists needs to be expedited. 

Council recessed at 10:13 p.m.

items.title: Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, provided a brief overview of public health activities for the month of June 2025. She highlighted that there has been a decline in local measles activity with only 110 cases total since March 2025 and there have been no new cases since early June 2025. Public Health continues to work with local partners, specifically with organizations that coordinate summer school and camp programs to promote proactive measures to minimize operational disruptions if there was a case of measles. She reminded the community that the most effective way to prevent measles and its complications is to get the measle vaccination. 

Received for information.

items.title: PDL-CAS-25-010, 2026 Council and Committee Meeting Calendar
notes:
T. Brubacher provided a brief overview of the annual Council and Committee Meeting Calendar, specifically that past practices of holding Committee days on Tuesdays and Council meetings on Wednesdays has continued with consideration for municipal events such as the Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference. He noted that the calendar was circulated to all area municipal clerks in May 2025 and staff did not receive feedback until June 23, 2025. The City of Cambridge Clerk requested that the Region consider holding Committee meetings on any other day than Tuesdays to avoid conflicts with Cambridge Council meetings.

T. Brubacher confirmed that the Regional inaugural meeting following the 2026 election has been scheduled for December 2026 to all for area municipalities to hold their inaugural meetings beforehand. 

J. Liggett presented an amendment to the staff recommendation to reschedule Committee meetings from Tuesdays to the corresponding Wednesdays. 

Councillors C. James and M. Harris expressed concern with rescheduling the days of these meetings as the schedule was set prior to the 2022 election, there should be consistency in scheduling, and other Members of Council have previous commitments scheduled for Wednesdays. They further highlighted that Councillor that are directly elected are considered part-time employees. They also suggested that there are staff and administrative considerations and that this adjustment should be postponed for consideration until the next term of Council.

J. Nowak also indicated that holding Commitee meetings during the day on Wednesdays would cause conflicts for the Township of Wellesley meeting calendar.

Council discussed the recommendation being deferred to allow City of Cambridge staff to look at options for rescheduling their meeting calendar.

notes:

Brubacher provided a brief overview of the report PDL-CAS-25-011, Declaration of Vacant Regional Councillor - Kitchener and Considerations to Fill the Position and recognized the passing of Councillor K. Williams. He informed Council that the Municipal Act requires that the K. Williams' seat be declared vacant by the second Council meeting held following the passing of a Councillor. He explained that following the declaration of the vacant position, Council needs to determine how to fill the position based on the options outlined in the above noted report. 

Council discussed and deliberated on the options provided by staff and selected option 1B which would be appointment by call of application. The process was amended by Council to schedule the Special Council meeting to hear from Applicants from August 20, 2025, to August 14, 2025, which resulted in two further amendments in that the application deadline was changed to August 1, 2025, and that the applications would be made available to Council and the public by August 6, 2025.

items.title: Notice of Motion
notes:
Regional Chair K. Redman provided the following motion to be considered at the Council Meeting to be held on August 27, 2025:

WHEREAS Waterloo Region is quickly growing to a community of one-million people;

WHEREAS the Waterloo Region Health Network (WRHN) is working with all partners to establish a new acute care hospital situated at Bearinger Drive in the City of Waterloo and;

WHEREAS Region of Waterloo Council is working diligently to balance the critical needs of our growing community and future affordability;

WHEREAS The Local Share Plan, public engagement framework, and the impacts of the hospital on Regional services have yet to be identified with the WRHN;

THEREFORE IT BE RESOLVED

THAT staff work with WRHN and report back on the impacts of the new hospital on the region, and inform on lifecycle benefits and costs to the Region, including impacts on key services such as paramedics, public health, transit and water

THAT staff develop a funding and contribution policy framework to guide Regional Council’s decision-making process for the funding of the new hospital and future requests for hospital expansions

THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present its initial Local Share Plan and overall Total Project Costs to Regional Council as soon as possible, and

THAT the Region of Waterloo formally requests that WRHN present a community-wide engagement plan to Region of Waterloo Council as the process of building a new hospital in Waterloo Region advances.

motions.item_title: PDL-CAS-25-008, Code of Conduct Update
motions.text: Amendment That subsection 5.1 item f) " they shall use Staff resources and time effectively, which includes but is not limited to only referring essential matters to Staff for reports;" of the Council-Staff Relations policy be removed That in subsection 5.1 item j) of the Council-Staff Relations policy, the word shall be changed to may so that it reads "They may request advice from the Clerk about the appropriate wording of motions, amendments, and formal directions of Staff that will be placed before Council to consider and discuss;" That a section be added to the Council-Staff Relations policy stating that "this policy should at minimum be reviewed at Regional Administration and Finance Committee and finally approved by council once per term, in the first year of a new term"; and That in Section 8.2 of the Code of Conduct the sentences “Members are only entitled to information in the possession of the Region that is relevant to matters before the Council, or a committee. Otherwise, Members enjoy the same access rights to information as any other member of the community or resident of the Region and must follow the same processes as any private person to obtain such information.” be removed and replaced by the following “Members of Council shall not access or attempt to gain access to confidential information in the possession of the Region unless it is necessary for the performance of their duties and not prohibited by Regional policy.”

motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve the proposed Code of Conduct and Council-staff relations policy as outlined in Appendices B & C respectively of report PDL-CAS- 25-008, dated May 21, 2025, with the following amendments:

  • That subsection 5.1 item f) " they shall use Staff resources and time effectively, which includes but is not limited to only referring essential matters to Staff for reports;" of the Council-Staff Relations policy be removed
